extraction_metadata.extraction_notes: Vector table with a clean text layer. Rule-line geometry recovered from a 200 dpi raster render gives 13 vertical rules (1 label column + 11 timepoint columns) and only three horizontal rules (table top, below the header row, table bottom), i.e. exactly one body row. Marks binned to the timepoint columns from pdftotext -bbox token centres and diffed against a visual read. One leading label column (L=1); first data column is position 2.

table_metadata.table_title: Schedule of Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Assessments on Days 1, 25, 29, and 39
table_metadata.table_purpose: Hour-by-hour PK/PD blood sampling timepoints on Days 1, 25, 29 and 39 for the PK and PD sampling activities that appear as single rows in Table 1.
table_metadata.notes: Classified 'subsidiary': the columns are a finer timing grid (hours post-dose) than Table 1's day columns, and the table gives detailed timing for a subset of Table 1's activities - Table 1 footnote o says 'See Table 2 for PK/PD sampling on Days 1, 25, 29, and 39' and footnote p points at the same table. It is not a track (same participants, same treatment period) and not a reference table (its rows are assessments performed on participants). STRUCTURE NOTE: the source prints ONE rule-bounded body cell whose text is four lines naming TWO assessments ('Blood sampling for PK: Plasma total Mo and PUF-Mo' and 'PD: Plasma total and PUF-Cu, LBC, ceruloplasmin, ceruloplasmin-bound Cu'), with a single row of marks vertically centred across all four lines. The two assessments are separate activity rows in Table 1, so they are emitted here as two activities (row_position 2 and 3) and the centred marks are applied to both, per the vertically-merged-mark convention. No horizontal rule separates the two names - that is an extraction decision, not a printed row split.

schedule_properties.property_comment: Printed row label 'Time point (hours)' carrying footnote marker a. Values are clock hours relative to dosing (−0.5, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 24). Typed 'timepoint' because the values are within-visit times post-dose, not days or visits.

annotations.annotation_text: Time points are relative to dosing (0 hours).
Hour 24 PK/PD sampling is to occur just prior to the next-day dose of ALXN1840.

Note: Windows for PK/PD time points will be defined as ±10% of the nominal time point. On Days 1 and 39, triplicate 12-lead ECG will be collected at 4 hours postdose. When multiple procedures are scheduled to occur at the same time, the following order of events should be strictly adhered to whenever possible: ECG, vital signs, blood sampling (eg, for PK/PD), study intervention administration, and meal.
